messages:
maria: heads up — GPU attach latency in ap-east-1 is spiking, several batch jobs stuck in PROVISIONING >3m. I'm seeing NVMe errors on a subset of nodes in pool-gpu-a :warning:

oncall-bot: alert: nvme_error_rate > 5% in ap-east-1 (avg over 5m). Affected cohort: pool-gpu-a. Incident ticket opened automatically.

alex: quick check of dmesg from node-az3-04 shows repeated crc/io errors on nvme0n1 and device reset loops:
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[ 1234.568012] nvme nvme0: ATA crc error, p1
[ 1234.568345] nvme nvme0: controller reset failed
```

jordan: can we drain affected nodes and reprovision? concern: mass drain will drop available GPUs and backlog will spike.

maria: planning incremental drains. I'll cordon 3 nodes at a time, kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node-az3-04 then run nvme-cli checks and a quick fio sanity. don't want full pool eviction.

sam: confirming scrub jobs started around 03:00 UTC in ap-east-1. scrub concurrency + heavy autoscaler churn may be amplifying write pressure. Did we just collide janitor window with a scale event?

alex: looks like scrub throughput peaked at the same time as a 2x autoscaler event — contention on local NVMe caused a sharp rise in queue depth and some drives returned media errors. short-term mitigation: throttle scrub concurrency and pause aggressive janitor passes for 30m.

jordan: also propose adding a scheduler predicate to avoid scheduling new GPU pods to nodes with smart attr 197 (pending wear) above threshold. I can push a canary patch for the provisioner.

maria: canary patch applied to ap-east-1 control-plane-canary. Also quarantining nodes showing >3 SMART error counters and replacing them from standby. Running:
```
sudo smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 | egrep "(critical_warning|data_units_written|media_error_count)"
nvme list && nvme error-log /dev/nvme0n1 | tail -n 50
```

storage-bot: action items: INC-1234 created. Quarantined nodes: node-az3-04, node-az3-07, node-az3-11. Autoscaler diverted 12 pending pods to us-east-1 fallback pool.

sam: cost note — diverting to fallback regions increases GPU-hour spend ~18% for the impacted batches. Ops accept? we should notify product about delayed SLAs.

maria: approved for 30m emergency diversion to protect throughput. We'll capture exact spend in the incident ticket. Monitoring attach latency; will escalate to postmortem if >200ms median after mitigations. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jordan: once we've stabilized I can follow up with a small scheduler RFC to filter nodes by nvme health metrics before scheduling GPU attachments.

maria: closing this thread for now — reopen if errors recur. We'll attach logs and timelines to INC-1234.
